blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses ensure their financial statements reflect the true financial position at year-end?

blocks.markdown: In accounting, it is crucial to match income and expenses to the period they belong to, ensuring accurate financial reporting. This is where accruals and prepayments come into play.

blocks.title: Accruals and Prepayments
blocks.text: An accrual is an expense or income that has been incurred or earned but not yet paid or received. A prepayment is an expense paid in advance or income received in advance.

blocks.markdown: Accruals and prepayments are adjustments made to the financial statements to ensure that all income and expenses are recorded in the period they relate to. This is in line with the accrual basis of accounting.

blocks.title: Adjusting for Accruals and Prepayments
blocks.prompt: Imagine a business pays its rent annually in advance on January 1st. How should this be adjusted in the accounts at year-end?

steps.text: Identify the total rent paid in advance at the start of the year.
Calculate the portion of rent that applies to the current accounting period.
Adjust the accounts to reflect the prepayment for the next period.

blocks.answer: The rent covering the next year is recorded as a prepayment in the balance sheet.

blocks.markdown: Accruals are recorded as liabilities on the balance sheet because they represent expenses that are owed. Prepayments, on the other hand, are recorded as assets because they represent expenses paid in advance.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check the accounting period in question when adjusting for accruals and prepayments to ensure accurate financial statements.

points: Accruals and prepayments are essential for matching income and expenses to the correct period.
Accruals are recorded as liabilities, while prepayments are recorded as assets on the balance sheet.
